question: Find one thing in the archive that was agreed and then never done. Show the trail from the agreement to the present, and say who would have needed to notice.

answer.text: The clearest example of an agreement that was never carried out is the quarterly business review written into the SOW as an obligation. On 2024-06-11 Robert Kahn demanded it: "Put the quarterly review in the SOW... Not as a nice idea, basically as an obligation" , and Marco Rossi accepted: "We will put it in" . The trail then goes quiet for almost a year. At the 90-day business review on 2025-05-22, Lena Fischer notes the SOW agreed quarterly cadence but "this is the first one" and it "has felt ad hoc" [, , ]; Marco accepts to formalise the cadence . On 2025-06-24 Ana Duarte reports the cadence has now been set up — quarterly, next in September — so the original SOW obligation was left unformalised for roughly a year, and the archive contains no record that the SOW wording itself was ever amended. Who would have needed to notice: Marco Rossi, who accepted the SOW wording on 2024-06-11, and Robert Kahn, who demanded it as an obligation and attended the 90-day review where the gap surfaced. Recommendation: treat the 2025-06-24 cadence setup as the compensating control and confirm in writing whether the SOW text was ever changed, since the archive shows only the meeting-level agreement, not a document amendment.
